big_case.notes: First district court preliminary injunction blocking IIRIRA section 102(c) border-barrier waivers in two decades, halting construction across the 517-mile Big Bend Sector (including Big Bend National Park) under the $46.5B OBBBA appropriation, and eliciting a published per curiam Supreme Court opinion holding under Dalton v. Specter, Biden v. Nebraska, and FCC v. Consumers' Research that there is no such thing as a 'constitutional' major-questions claim within section 102(c)(2)(A)'s jurisdiction-stripping exception.

central_claims.basis: On November 9, 2026, the Court granted an unqualified stay of the Western District of Texas preliminary injunction pending the filing and disposition of a timely certiorari petition, declining summary reversal.
central_claims.claim: The Court will grant the Solicitor General's application for an unqualified stay of the preliminary injunction pending certiorari and decline summary reversal.

central_claims.basis: Justice Alito referred Application 26A560 to the full Court on November 9, 2026, no further response request occurred, no additional amicus briefs were filed (`amicus_briefs: 1`), the Government filed its reply on October 30, 2026, and the Court issued its order on November 9, 2026.
central_claims.claim: Justice Alito will refer the application to the full Court (97%), no additional amicus briefs will likely be filed (65% probability of no increment), the Solicitor General will file a reply around October 30-31, and the Court will issue its order between November 3 and November 9, 2026.

central_claims.basis: The November 9, 2026 per curiam opinion (`writings/OT2026-2/01-per-curiam.txt`) held that the Government is exceedingly likely to prevail because IIRIRA section 102(c)(2)(A) limits district court jurisdiction to constitutional claims, respondents' major-questions claim alleges only that the Secretary exceeded statutory authority under Dalton v. Specter, 511 U.S. 462, 472-474 (1994), and 'there is no such thing as a 'constitutional' major-questions claim.'
central_claims.claim: If the Court issues a brief per curiam explanation, its primary ground will be that IIRIRA section 102(c)(2)(A) and Dalton v. Specter, 511 U.S. 462 (1994), bar district court jurisdiction because respondents' major-questions challenge is a statutory ultra vires claim rather than a constitutional claim.

central_claims.basis: The per curiam opinion rested its merits holding strictly on the section 102(c)(2)(A) jurisdictional bar without reaching whether the Big Bend projects satisfy section 102(a) on the merits or invoking Trump v. CASA on remedial overbreadth, while holding that the balance of equities and irreparable harm (border security under Von Raab, nonrecoverable daily contractor costs under NIH v. APHA, and Congress's statutory balance in section 102(c)(1) under Oakland Cannabis and Winter) favored a stay.
central_claims.claim: The Court's reasoning will also hold that the balance of equities and irreparable harm favor staying an injunction halting border-security infrastructure, and will address section 102(a)/102(c)(1) statutory authority and remedial overbreadth under Trump v. CASA.

central_claims.basis: The Court issued a per curiam opinion rather than an unexplained order, only Justice Jackson noted that she would deny the application for stay (Justices Sotomayor and Kagan did not note dissents), and no Justice authored a separate concurrence or dissent.
central_claims.claim: The order will most likely (~65%) issue without an authored opinion (or with a dissent by Justice Sotomayor or Justice Jackson), with Justices Sotomayor, Kagan, and Jackson noting dissents.
